name: Indonesian
modelReview: artifacts only, no renderer yet: written 2026-11-19 by Claude Fable 5.2 from usage notes written in Indonesian with no knowledge of cron; a rule book (answers.md) derived from them, a lexicon, and hand-written rows (87 visible, 153 held out, 360 hard cases, 38 option rows), none produced by running a renderer. The rows pass the grid oracle (coverage, no duplicate, equal schedules worded alike). Read once, 2026-11-19, by a blind judge briefed only in Indonesian (114 sentences, every reading of each) and by an adversarial schedule read of all 637 rows; no row stated a wrong schedule under its intended reading, three sentences had a real second reading and several devices a weak one. Revised the same day on those reads: no «ke-0» and no minute named as a stretch; the «pada jam yang dimulai pukul», «berulang setiap», «masing-masing … sepanjang menit itu» and «… dan setiap N bulan sesudahnya» devices removed; a month or year of a union after «keduanya»; conditions said positively («tetapi … hanya jika jatuh pada»); a count back from the month's end said as its date where the date is fixed; a run of weekdays with no «setiap» and wherever it lies in the week; hour 0 on the 12-hour clock as «12 dini hari». About 240 rows changed. A second blind judge then read 69 changed sentences (2026-11-19) and found second readings in the seconds with no minute named, a stretch end that was not the last firing, the rhythm of years, a whole hour said as minutes 0 to 59, and a union with a trailing condition; a second revision the same day cured each (the minute always named; «terakhir pukul»; «setiap tahun ke-N sesudahnya»; lengths such as «selama 1 menit» and «selama 30 menit pertama»; «pada jam genap / ganjil» for every second hour, adopted as plainly understood with no corpus hit; union arms said positively and joined by «, dan juga»; a moved date's clause after the time). About 170 rows changed again; those forms have had no independent read, and nothing has had a native read. Devices with no corpus support found: «pada jam genap», «setiap N jam mulai pukul» with several first times, «tiap kali», «setelah pukul», «keduanya pada», «setiap tahun ke-N sesudahnya», «digeser ke hari …»; the parts of the day of the 12-hour style have no official bounds and are the author's. A renderer was then built from the artifacts by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row (153 of 153 held-out rows on its first judged run), and audited the same day by Claude Fable 5.2 (some 600 rendered patterns read against an independent answer key, plus 54 000 random renderings for faults of form): no sentence stated a wrong set of times; repaired were a moved date's clause that trailed a union with nothing to say what moves, a last firing named without its second, dates named that a counted weekday cannot fall on, a run of weekdays less a day where four names serve, doubled «tiap kali», and nine single times where a run and a rhythm of hours serve; the rule book now states the rules the builder had to guess. The repaired forms have had no independent read
